mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to lower corporate profit margins and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during sustained INDPRO contractions relative to its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the Retail Sales Index (RSAFS) and Housing Starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both > 12-month moving average simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL (consumer price index) below 2% for two consecutive months, coupled with a stable or rising FEDFUNDS rate, signals disinflation with restrictive policy, which compresses earnings growth and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS stable or rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two months and FEDFUNDS is stable or rising.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month, combined with an unemployment rate below 4%, signals an overheating labor market that precedes a policy tightening, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: overheating labor market before policy tightening
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS jumps by >1% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly rebound in real GDP (GDPC1) after two consecutive declines signals a recovery from recession, which boosts investor optimism and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous quarter AND previous two quarters were declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive following a two-quarter GDP contraction and a subsequent quarterly rebound.
